newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA proposes changes to current dealing for RTGS.
newsitem.headline: RBA proposes changes to current dealing for RTGS.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has proposed some changes to its current dealing arrangements to help avoid any disruption to market conditions due to the introduction of real time gross settlement (RTGS).

The changes, to take effect from October 1, will include an end-of-day repurchase agreement (repo) facilty and a reduction in the interest rate paid on the balances held in bank's exchange settlement accounts (ESAs), the RBA said.

While RTGS is not due to be fully implemented until April 1998, the RBA said it saw merit in implementing changes, which had been decided after wide consultation with market participants, well ahead of this to help smooth the transition.

The RBA's current arrangements of announcing its money market position and dealing intentions at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) and dealing between 10.00 a.m. and 10.30 a.m. (2400 GMT and 0030 GMT) would remain suitable under RTGS.
While the morning operations would remain the RBA's principal vehicle for achieving its cash rate target, under RTGS a further round of dealing may be rquired, it said.
This was because the system cash figure will be an estimate, rather than a figure derived from overnight clearing streams as at present, and was therefore subject to forecasting error.

"Under RTGS, it is possible that market pressures could emerge toward the end of the settlement day as banks and others with ESAs balance their liquidity positions and bid for funds to unwind intra-day repos," the RBA said.
To avoid any possible market disruption, the RBA will now provide ESA holders an end-of-day facility.
"The facility will take ther form of overnight repos at 25 basis points over the target cash rate," it said.
The RBA said it was seeking to strike a balance between providing a degree of certainty about of end-of-day funding, while retaining the incentive to settle in the marketplace.

The facility will be available only to those with ESAs and limited to after 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) when RITS (Reserve Bank Information and Transfer System) is closed to non-exchange settlement transactions.

The RBA also said it had noted some concerns that current arrangements where an interest rate 10 points under the target rate was paid on the balances of ESA accounts did not provide enough incentive to lend surplus funds back into the market.
Consistent with this was the strong growth in ESA balances since the current arrangements were introduced, the RBA said.
The margin under the cash rate target would therefore be widened to 25 basis points, the RBA said.

The new measures was expected to help further develop the money market by encouraging borrowers to seek market funds before using the end-of-day-repo facility, while also providing an incentive for those with surplus funds to lend them.
"This should also enhance market liquidity during the day by providing incentives to settle as early as possible and minimise the need to use Reserve Bank facilities," the RBA said.
Other aspects of market operations will remain unchanged.

"Specifically, except for the end of day facility, eligibility to deal with the Bank will remain open to all RITS members, and the present rediscount facility for Treasury notes within 90 days to maturity will continued to be offered as a safety-valve for the system more generally," the RBA said.
The intra-day credit facility, where the RBA could deal more than once in a day, will not become operational until RTGS begins, which is currently seen as June 1998.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
